column8: Verification really is off and this really is TOFU. Safe to ship because the connection carries nothing and grants nothing: the request is an unauthenticated GET of /api/bmc?opt=get&type=about, VerifyPeerCertificate only RECORDS the fingerprint and always returns nil, and the captured digest is shown to the operator to confirm against the board before it becomes the pin NewTuringPiBackend enforces. TRIP-WIRE: void if this probe ever sends credentials, or if its result configures anything without the operator confirming the digest.

Certificate pinning is STRICTER than the CA trust being skipped: CA trust accepts any cert a trusted issuer signed, pinnedCertVerifier accepts exactly one SHA-256 fingerprint. Skipping is also not optional - the board mints a self-signed cert at the epoch, so it is permanently expired and no chain check can pass. TRIP-WIRE: safety lives on the NEXT line (tlsCfg.VerifyPeerCertificate = pinnedCertVerifier). If that assignment is removed, made conditional, or replaced with a partial comparison, this becomes accept-any-certificate and this fingerprint will NOT catch it.

Genuine log forging: the channel query parameter reaches log.Printf unescaped, and a newline in it forges log lines that feed Loki and the IDS drawer. Independently confirmed - gosec already flagged this exact file under G706 and #145 names flash_handlers.go among its thirteen sites. MEDIUM, so it does not block a release; it is tracked debt with a fix owed, not an accepted finding.

The input is not a password. GenerateToken is the only source of what is hashed and it produces 32 bytes from crypto/rand - 256 bits, hex-encoded. Slow KDFs exist to make brute-force expensive against LOW-entropy human-chosen secrets; a 256-bit random token has no searchable keyspace, so argon2/bcrypt would buy nothing and would add cost to every bus authentication. TRIP-WIRE: void the moment HashToken is called on an operator-typed secret. Callers today are GenerateToken and mint, both hashing freshly generated bytes.

False on two independent grounds. (1) No secret is present: the preauth entries Compile builds carry metadata only - name, user, reusable, ephemeral, expiresIn, tags - and key material never enters the map. CodeQL tainted on the identifier NAME, not a value. (2) Not password hashing: this is a change-detection fingerprint reconcile compares desired against observed with, and nothing is ever verified against it. TRIP-WIRE: ground 1 holds only while the compiled state stays metadata-only; adding a real key or token to it re-opens this.

The scheme is not attacker-reachable: the template literal hard-codes an http:// prefix, so the value can never begin with javascript: or data:, which is the only route from URL to script execution. firewallHost is operator-typed only - useState(empty), set solely by this input onChange - and the API-derived nodeId feeds the PLACEHOLDER, which is inert. TRIP-WIRE: the file comment says host derivation becomes automatic when primaryLanIp lands on Node; on that day this value becomes NODE-SUPPLIED and this verdict must be re-opened. The hard-coded scheme still caps it at open-redirect, not XSS.

The flagged line is the tar reader's Next() in extractIdentity; the entry name it yields is refused before any file-system operation if it contains `..` or starts with `/` (the explicit guard immediately below the source line, in the shape this query recognises), then again by validateRestorePath, which requires a clean relative path of [A-Za-z0-9._-] components and rejects `.`/`..`/empty components. The only sinks are backupxfer/fsat primitives — openat(2) relative to the staging directory's fd with O_NOFOLLOW, one component at a time, fstat'd — so no name can leave the staging directory by traversal or by symlink. Every member is further bounded to the size the authenticated in-archive manifest names and verified against its sha256. TRIP-WIRE: the guard lives on the lines after the flagged one; deleting it does not move this fingerprint. Exercised by TestPrepareRestoreRefusesHostileMembers (dot-dot, absolute, symlink, unlisted member) which assert the data dir is untouched.

OpenDir's Openat takes ONE path component relative to an already-opened directory fd with O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY, then fstats and requires a directory: the kernel resolves the name beneath that fd and a symlink in it is ELOOP, so the primitive can only ever open a child of the fd it was handed, never a path. Whether a caller may name that child is the caller's shape check — the restore validates archive members and generation ids (validateRestorePath, proto.BackupValidGenerationID) and the ingest endpoint validates member paths by shape (proto.BackupValidMemberPath) before calling it. The taint CodeQL follows is the tar entry name the restore has already refused if it contains `..`. Covered by backupxfer/fsat tests (symlink refused at every position) and the restore's hostile-member cases.
